title: Schalke relegated from Bundesliga: A Royal Case of the Blues
content: # Schalke relegated from Bundesliga: A Royal Case of the Blues. Schalke have been relegated from the Bundesliga. It's a story of sporting failure, mismanagement, pandemic-related scandal and the power of one man. With over 160,000 members, Schalke 04 are the second-biggest football club in Germany, seven times German champions and one of the biggest names in world football. But now, for the first time in 33 years, the *Königsblauen* (Royal Blues) have been relegated to the second division. It's a journey which has left Schalke with €217 million ($257.8 million) of debt, an inexperienced coach, a squad unfit for the second division, a supervisory board divided in acrimony, a thoroughly disillusioned fanbase and a list of intrigues to rival any Netflix drama. But, for Kornelia Toporzysek, a lifelong Schalke supporter, lawyer and former member of the club's honorary board, it was August 7, 2019, the day on which her fellow board members acquitted Clemens Tönnies of racism.

title: Is this the year Schalke make it back to the Bundesliga?
content: Miron Muslić (l.) has led Schalke to 12 wins already this season and ensured the team will end 2025 in pole position for promotion. # Is this the year Schalke make it back to the Bundesliga? Schalke have been languishing at the wrong end of the Bundesliga 2 table since their last relegation from the top flight two years ago, but under the stewardship of head coach Miron Muslić, the Royal Blues finally appear to be back on the right track in the push for a Bundesliga return. Steeped in history and tradition, the Bundesliga co-founders have won seven German titles, five DFB Cups and a UEFA Cup. And despite their recent struggles - with relegations in 2021 and 2023 - they remain one of the country’s best supported clubs with over 200,000 members, surpassed only by Bayern Munich and fierce rivals Borussia Dortmund. Since their relegation on the final day of the 2022/23 season, *Die Knappen* have only managed 10th- and 14th-placed finishes in Bundesliga 2, begging the question: when will Schalke play in the Bundesliga again?

German Football Disasters presents Schalke 04. Second in the Bundesliga in 2018 and in the Champions League the following year. By April 2021, relegated.

0:00 Introduction: from Champions League contenders to Bundesliga footnote
0:50 The Heidel era: how a celebrated sporting director dismantled a squad (2016–2019)
2:40 The Man City humiliation: 7-0 at the Etihad, 10-2 on aggregate, and the rot confirmed
3:45 David Wagner and the COVID collapse: a 16-game winless run and a chairman's resignation
4:40 Clemens Tönnies: the slaughterhouse outbreak, 1,500 infected workers, and the exit
5:50 The 2020-21 season begins: 8-0 at Bayern Munich
7:00 Manuel Baum, Tasmania Berlin's record, and the Hoppe miracle
8:30 Christian Gross, the Bielefeld relegation, and the bus attack
9:40 The final reckoning: three wins, 86 goals conceded

THE SCHALKE COLLAPSE EXPLAINED:
- At the time of relegation in 2021, Schalke had around 155,000 registered members — one of the largest clubs in Germany — and had played in the Champions League as recently as 2018-19
- Sporting Director Christian Heidel (appointed February 2016) oversaw a transfer policy that let academy product Max Meyer (after his public criticism of Heidel) and star midfielder Leon Goretzka leave on free transfers in summer 2018, with neither replaced at equivalent quality
- Schalke's 2018-19 season dropped them from 2nd to 14th in the Bundesliga, just five points above direct relegation, before elimination from the Champions League Round of 16 by Manchester City (7-0 at the Etihad on 12 March 2019, 10-2 on aggregate); Tedesco was sacked 14 March 2019 and Heidel stepped down the same week
- Schalke entered 2020-21 with debts exceeding €200m, no European football income, and a manager on an 18-game winless run (combining the 16 from 2019-20 with the opening two games of the new season); their first match: 8-0 at Bayern Munich on 18 September 2020
- Five managers across the season: David Wagner (sacked 27 September), Manuel Baum (sacked 18 December), Huub Stevens for nine days as interim over Christmas, Christian Gross (relieved 28 February 2021), and Dimitrios Grammozis to close the season
- Schalke reached 30 consecutive Bundesliga games without a win before a 4-0 victory over Hoffenheim on 9 January 2021 ended the streak — one short of Tasmania Berlin's all-time record of 31 (set in 1965-66); the win was powered by a Matthew Hoppe hat-trick, the first Bundesliga hat-trick by an American player
- Relegation confirmed 20 April 2021, 1-0 at Arminia Bielefeld (Fabian Klos, 50'), with four games still to play — ending 30 consecutive seasons in the Bundesliga, their first relegation since 1988

Why did one of Germany's great clubs — seven national titles, one UEFA Cup, Champions League semi-finalists as recently as 2011 — go from second in the Bundesliga in 2018 to relegation by April 2021? 

The answer starts not in the dressing room but in the boardroom, with a transfer policy under Christian Heidel that sold quality and spent the proceeds on older, lower-calibre players who did not replace what was lost. By the end of 2018-19, the squad that had finished second had collapsed to 14th, and the Champions League campaign ended 10-2 on aggregate to Manchester City. Heidel and manager Domenico Tedesco departed within days of each other in March 2019.

The financial damage ran deeper than the football. Chairman Clemens Tönnies had funded much of Schalke's ambition and personally negotiated the Gazprom sponsorship deal with Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin. His position became untenable in June 2020 when a COVID-19 outbreak at his Rheda-Wiedenbrück meat-processing plant infected more than 1,500 workers and triggered a full regional lockdown. He resigned within days, removing the club's primary financial backer at precisely the moment their debts had reached €200m, their European income had dried up, and the pandemic was cutting matchday revenue by €2m per home game.

David Wagner steadied things briefly in 2019-20 before a 16-game winless run ended his tenure after the opening two matches of 2020-21. What followed across that season was a cascade of managerial appointments, dressing room confrontations, and results that brought Schalke within one match of Tasmania Berlin's 55-year-old record for consecutive games without a Bundesliga win. When 19-year-old Matthew Hoppe scored a hat-trick to beat Hoffenheim 4-0 on 9 January 2021, ending 30 winless games in one afternoon, it briefly felt like a turning point. It was not. Three wins from 34 games, 86 goals conceded, and relegation confirmed with four games to spare on 20 April 2021.
